drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: For discussion and subject to client approval, we propose a $400,000 annual Base Salary, eligibility for an annual performance bonus targeted at 50% of Base Salary, and participation in the Company’s executive benefit plans. We can accept your proposed 24-month severance framework, subject to the attached payment and benefits provisions. We have deleted the non-compete and added narrowly drawn cause and good-reason definitions with notice and cure protections. These proposals remain subject to agreement on definitive documentation.

edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. Proposed terms, subject to client approval: The Executive shall receive an annual Base Salary of $400,000, payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices, and shall be eligible for an annual performance bonus targeted at 50% of Base Salary, based on performance objectives established reasonably and in good faith by the Board. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the health, retirement, disability, life insurance and other benefit plans generally available to similarly situated senior executives, subject to applicable plan terms, and shall receive four weeks of paid vacation annually.

3. SEVERANCE. Proposed terms, subject to client approval: Upon termination by the Company without Cause or resignation by the Executive for Good Reason, the Company shall pay accrued salary, earned but unpaid compensation and other vested entitlements when due and, subject to the Executive executing and not revoking a customary release of employment-related claims, provide severance equal to 24 months of Base Salary at the rate in effect immediately before termination, disregarding any reduction constituting Good Reason. Severance shall be paid in substantially equal installments over 24 months under regular payroll practices, beginning on the first payroll date after the release becomes effective, but no later than 60 days after termination, with the initial payment including installments otherwise due. If that 60-day period spans two calendar years, payments shall begin in the second year. For 24 months following termination, the Company shall also continue medical, dental and vision coverage for the Executive and eligible dependents on the same cost-sharing basis as immediately before termination; where continued participation is unavailable or impermissible, the Company shall provide a taxable monthly payment equal to its share of the premium for equivalent coverage. These benefits cease upon eligibility for equivalent coverage with a subsequent employer. Payments and benefits shall be administered consistently with applicable law, including Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code and any required six-month delay.

4. TERMINATION DEFINITIONS; NO NON-COMPETE. No post-employment non-compete shall apply. “Cause” means (a) conviction of, or a guilty or no-contest plea to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty; (b) willful fraud, embezzlement or material misappropriation involving the Company; or (c) willful misconduct or a willful material breach of this Agreement causing material harm to the Company. Cause excludes good-faith business judgments and failure to meet performance targets alone. Before termination for Cause, the Company shall provide reasonably detailed written notice and an opportunity for the Executive, with counsel, to respond to the Board. For conduct capable of cure, the Executive shall have 30 days after receipt of notice to cure. “Good Reason” means, without the Executive’s written consent, (i) a material reduction in Base Salary; (ii) a material diminution in authority, duties or responsibilities; (iii) relocation of the principal work location by more than 50 miles that materially increases the Executive’s commute; or (iv) a material breach of this Agreement by the Company. The Executive must notify the Company in writing within 90 days after the condition first occurs, allow 30 days after receipt for cure, and resign within 60 days after expiration of that cure period if the condition remains uncured.

receiver.message_back: Subject to our client’s approval and definitive documentation, we can proceed on the $400,000 salary, 50% target bonus, benefits, narrowed termination definitions and no non-compete, provided the 24-month severance includes target bonus as well as Base Salary, is not subject to mitigation or offset, and requires only a mutually agreed release containing no additional restrictive covenants. Please also provide that replacement medical, dental and vision payments preserve the agreed benefit after taxes and that coverage ends only when equivalent subsequent-employer coverage actually begins.
